input.query: why is the dependency fingerprint the same on every platform

results.snippet:
feat(build): the dependency fingerprint is the same on every platform

Every build key folds in a fingerprint of the installed dependency tree. It included the
packages npm installs on some platforms only (@esbuild/*, @cloudflare/workerd-*,
@number0/iroh-*, @img/sharp-*, ...), so the same code had different keys on Windows,
macOS and Linux and no build could be shared between them. Packages that declare os,
cpu or libc are now left out of the fold; the wrapper that selects one still pins its
exact version in its own manifest, which is folded. Encoding root-deps-v8 -> v9.

Checked on the installed node_modules of a real win32-x64 and darwin-arm64 package of
the same commit: the folded tree hashes differ without the filter (967fef57... vs
d1e0fc8a...) and are identical with it (839a8314... on both).

feat(release): a prepared workspace release is the same on every platform

The manifest records where it was produced instead of binding the platform and
architecture, and the shared cache key no longer includes them. This follows
from the platform-neutral dependency fingerprint.
Lunch is at noon on Thursday, the usual place.

fix(iroh): a peer cancelling a stream is not a failure of its session's retirement

A response written to a stream the peer had stopped with the protocol's own
cancel or session-close code failed with Stopped(513/514). That was recorded as
an outbound failure and made the session's retirement fail at every shutdown
with active requests. The garbage-collection failure that named four different
conditions by one message now names the one that held.

test: process death in tests is read from the process table, not from signal 0

Signalling a process with signal 0 succeeds for one that has died but not been reaped. A
zombie answers until its parent, or init once the parent is gone, collects it, which on a
loaded CI runner can take a moment. Tests that asserted a retired group or a left-over child
was gone with `process.kill(pid, 0)` therefore failed intermittently (hubServer,
launchTermination), though the process had exited.

One helper reads the process table and treats a zombie as gone. The tests whose subject is
a process that outlived its parent use it. deviceExecutors keeps signal 0 on purpose: its
child is the test's own, and the test waits for the parent to have reaped it.

Remove default timeouts — let agents take as long as they need

Timeouts are poison for agentic tasks. An agent doing a multi-step task
(load skill, read docs, write eval, run it, inspect results, retry) can
easily take minutes.

- waitForAgentMessage and waitForIdle default to no timeout (0 = wait
  indefinitely). The natural termination signal is the agent completing
  its turn (debounce-based idle detection) or disconnecting.
- Removed all per-test timeout fields from 15 test files.
- TestRunner no longer applies a 60s default — passes test.timeout
  through directly (undefined = no timeout).
- Timeout is still available as an opt-in per-test override for
  specific edge-case tests that intentionally test timeout behavior.
The default timeout for agent tests is 60 seconds; raise it per test if you need more.

Add pnpm natlang:vendor: pinned, verified natlang bundles for the templates

Stages natlang's workerd (TypeScript bundled in), dashboard and llama targets from
one natlang commit into Base and System, and --check (in check:commit) verifies each
vendored directory against its pin. The userland tsconfig reads .nl imports through
their generated .d.nl.ts declarations; the service-schema file census skips the
eval natlang provider contract, which is types, not a service table.

Add pnpm natlang:eval: run natlang evaluation suites from a host-owned projection

Stages the natlang eval bundle from a temporary worktree of origin/main (cached
by commit under .cache/natlang-eval), composes Base plus the template and its
projected npm dependencies as pnpm test:userland does, and drives natlang's
loadEvaluationSuite/evaluate with the suite's budget gateway. Everything the run
owns is retired under ownedEntry; results persist as JSON.

input.query: model gateway shutdown preparation kernel hold

results.snippet:
Let a failed shutdown preparation release the kernel hold, and admit host framework calls on service owners

A service-backed native owner (the model gateway) failed shutdown preparation because the host's durable-work release and native-invocation calls were not in its build catalog; the lifecycle then never reached the EvalDO release, whose held kernel-lease request waited forever on a release that did not come and blocked shutdown. Framework methods the host calls on every owner are now host-intrinsic, and the held kernel request ends when the host cancels its leg.

Fix workerd SIGKILL fallback: track exit observation, not proc.killed

`subprocess.killed` becomes true as soon as the signal is sent, not when
the child actually exits, so the previous guard never fired. Track exit
via the promise callback and SIGKILL only when the exit event did not
fire within the SIGTERM grace window. Also wait briefly for the SIGKILL
exit so the next respawn sees a fully released socket.

results.snippet:
fix(release): the npm smoke tests the installed package, and a written dist-tag is awaited

The smoke handed the installed server this checkout as its application root, so
its workspace runtime read prepared templates from the checkout, not the package.
A dist-tag read right after the write could still show the previous value; that
is now pending, as an unpublished version already is.

Treat a channel-less native owner as its own invocation trajectory
